candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — opioid conversion and overdose prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Use opioid equianalgesic conversions as estimates rather than exact switch doses and reduce the starting dose of the new opioid as clinically appropriate to account for incomplete cross-tolerance and patient variability.

options.A: Use the calculated equianalgesic dose without reduction because conversion factors fully account for cross-tolerance and individual response.
options.B: Increase the calculated dose of the new opioid because incomplete cross-tolerance makes the replacement opioid predictably less potent.
options.C: Treat the conversion as an estimate and generally start the new opioid below the calculated equivalent dose when appropriate because cross-tolerance and individual response vary.
options.D: Match the number and strength of tablets between opioids because equianalgesic estimates are unnecessary when both drugs are oral.

candidate.rationale: CDC states that equianalgesic/MME conversions are estimates and do not account for individual variability. The CDC table cautions not to use the calculated MME dose directly to determine the dose of a new opioid; the new opioid is typically dosed substantially lower to reduce overdose risk from incomplete cross-tolerance and variability. C is therefore the safest principle.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Opioid conversion estimates are not exact switch doses; the new opioid should generally be started below the calculated equivalent dose when clinically appropriate because incomplete cross-tolerance and individual variability increase overdose risk.
candidate.source_document_title: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain — United States, 2022
candidate.source_locator: MME conversion table cautions: equianalgesic conversions are estimates; do not use calculated MME dose directly when converting opioids; the new opioid is typically dosed substantially lower because of incomplete cross-tolerance and individual pharmacokinetic variability. Implementation considerations also advise reducing total daily dosage when changing opioids to account for incomplete cross-tolerance.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: November 4, 2022; current CDC guideline live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A client is being switched from one opioid to another. Which principle is safest when using an equianalgesic conversion estimate?
